hallOfFame.name: Deadpool (Series 6)
hallOfFame.why: One of the three most-desired Toy Biz figures; peak-nostalgia wave.

hallOfFame.name: Phoenix / Dark Phoenix (Series 6)
hallOfFame.why: Fan-favorite sculpt with rare variants; Hasbro later revisited her in the Queen Brood wave.

hallOfFame.name: Galactus BAF (Series 9, 2005)

hallOfFame.name: Sentinel BAF (Series 10, 2005)

hallOfFame.name: Apocalypse BAF (Series 12, 2006)

hallOfFame.name: Onslaught BAF (2006)

history.detail: Isaac Perlmutter's Toy Biz, successor to Charan/Chantex, holds the Marvel master toy license from 1990.
Marvel files for bankruptcy; Toy Biz merges with Marvel Entertainment Group to form Marvel Enterprises, Toy Biz becoming its toy division.

Marvel Legends launches as a Spider-Man Classics spin-off: clamshell packaging plus a 32-page reprint comic. Wave 1: Iron Man, Captain America, Hulk, Toad — aimed at adult collectors with best-in-class sculpt and articulation.
Series 9 (Galactus series) packs one piece of an 18" Galactus per figure — the Build-A-Figure is born. Followed by the Sentinel, Apocalypse, Giant-Man, Onslaught, Mojo and M.O.D.O.K.
Marvel terminates the Toy Biz Worldwide license a year early, paying a $13–16M penalty.
Marvel grants Hasbro a 5-year master toy license: $205M guaranteed royalties, $100M non-refundable advance. Retail sales begin Jan 1, 2007 with Ghost Rider and Spider-Man 3 lines.
New packaging drops the comic pack-in; new molds drop Toy Biz's signature finger joints. BAF continues with Annihilus, Brood Queen and others.
Announced at SDCC 2010 after fan demand and MCU momentum; all-new sculpts return January 2012.
Retooled as Marvel Legends: Infinite Series at $19.99 MSRP — box packaging, bigger BAFs, more accessories.
Photo-real face-printing for MCU likenesses; butterfly joints; pinless joints debut ~2020 and become standard.
First ML HasLab: 26.3" Sentinel at $349.99, funded in ~24 hours.
32" Galactus at $399.99 draws 14,000 backers — the biggest ML ever.
24" Giant-Man at $199.99 finishes with 13,876 backers. Ghost Rider's Engine of Vengeance becomes the line's only failed HasLab.
Standard MSRP reaches $24.99; deluxe $30–50; box sets $40–90; HasLab $200–400.
